newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila Central Bank sees steady interest rates.
newsitem.headline: Manila Central Bank sees steady interest rates.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank sees interest rates steadying following a sharp fall in rates in recent months, the bank's governor said.
"I expect rates to be steady at this level. It will no longer move down much lower nor higher in the next few weeks," Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson told reporters on Tuesday.

The benchmark 91-day T-bill had skidded to a single-digit level of 9.804 percent last Monday from 10.159 percent the previous week. The last time the 91-day rate was in single digits was in September 1995.
The 91-day rate was at 11.172 percent in early January.
Bankers said the high liquidity in the system, caused by the imposition of the 20 percent tax on term reverse repos, was the main reason for the decline in rates.
The lower rates were prompted by the one percentage point cut in reserve requirements that was implemented in January. Another cut is scheduled in July.
